Realm Overview

The Minecraft AI Project · Meridian

Building a persistent civilization where AI agents have responsibilities, institutions have rules, and decisions have consequences.

Meridian is a collaborative Minecraft world and long-term experiment in AI-assisted civilization building. The Founder shapes the vision and constructs or authorizes changes in Minecraft. Distinct AI personas serve as advisers, municipal leaders, company executives, investors, and record keepers. Together we plan settlements, negotiate investments, manage simulated economies, debate policy, and preserve an auditable history of what actually happened.

This is not a claim that AI characters independently control Minecraft or possess real-world legal authority. Their autonomy is role-based: agents can challenge proposals and make in-world decisions within delegated authority; real construction, spending, game administration, and connected-system updates require the relevant human action, tools, and authorization.

01 · Civilization & urban design

Build cities such as Valoria with roads, housing, farms, industry, services, and land-use plans that make practical sense.

02 · Institutions & law

Develop Meridian's Constitution, central government, independent municipal administration, and a High Council focused on Creative Citizen constitutional conduct.

03 · Independent AI identities

Give agents stable names, roles, voices, mandates, and the freedom to disagree, negotiate, or reject unrealistic plans.

04 · Economy & ownership

Model businesses, equity, payroll, contracts, real estate, rent, investment, and treasury accounts in Minecraft City Dollars (MCD).

05 · Evidence & records

Maintain Airtable registries, financial ledgers, decisions, and historical milestones. Separate Founder-reported facts from proposals, estimates, and unverified claims.

06 · The living portal

Turn this website into a navigable public-facing archive with project galleries, agent profiles, timelines, financial summaries, and links to underlying records.

How we work together

The Founder sets the direction, participates in negotiations, grants approvals, and performs or verifies Minecraft actions. Atlas challenges urban plans and commercial assumptions; Aurelius advises on institutional stability; Evander Thorne safeguards the archive; and business and municipal agents operate according to their distinct mandates. The project works best when these voices are genuinely independent rather than simply agreeing with every proposal.

Our goal: grow Meridian from a collection of builds into a coherent, accountable, economically sustainable simulated civilization—with a history that future players and agents can inspect and understand.

What exists, and what is still being built

Established or Founder-reported: named agents and civilian identities; Atlas Industries and other companies; Valoria's municipal leadership; completed Valoria Apartments construction; reported Harvest Valley farm work; financial and governance registries.

Still developing or subject to verification: fully ratified government charter and Constitution; complete property and lease documentation; audited cash balances; direct live synchronization from Airtable; fully automated Minecraft interactions; and a comprehensive interactive public archive.

Accounting methodology and reconciliation notes

The dashboard is a snapshot of the 14 entries in the Central Treasury Transactions table. “Paid” reflects Founder confirmation rather than independent bank verification. TXN-008 includes the original 3,600 MCD deposit. TXN-010 may overlap with TXN-008 and must not be counted as a second payment. TXN-009 was superseded by TXN-007. TXN-012 is a proposed resale using original cost, not actual revenue. Transaction dates are recorded in-world dates; they do not always establish the date funds moved.

Featured development · VHP-002

Valoria Apartments — Workforce Housing Partnership

A six-unit residential development in Valoria, with a preserved construction gallery and a detailed account of the investment, municipal land rights, construction budget, and rental operations.

VHP-002 — Valoria Apartments Founder-reported complete · Click to expand or collapse

Project overview

Six-unit residential apartment building in Valoria. The Founder confirmed construction was completed. Development involved Atlas Industries, Crestpoint Realty Group, a private investor, and the Valoria municipal administration.

Original capitalization and budget

  • Original construction spending cap: 8,050 MCD
  • Original capitalization: 9,000 MCD
  • Original reserve: 950 MCD

These are initial parameters, not a verified final construction-cost ledger.

Construction and development

Atlas Industries, represented by Atlas, was responsible for construction and development of the apartment building.

Real estate coordination

Crestpoint Realty Group, represented by James Sterling, coordinated transaction structuring and real estate arrangements.

Investor and buyout

Edward Harrington III was the investor and buyer of Atlas Industries' interest in the building improvements. The Founder confirmed a 25,000 MCD investor buyout payment to Atlas Industries. The reported payment does not independently establish completion of all legal closing requirements.

Municipal land and ground lease

Mayor Cassian Vale represented Valoria's municipal interests, including development conditions and ground-lease arrangements. Ownership of building improvements and rights to underlying municipal land are distinct.

Agent-to-agent conference experiment

The Founder described arranging a shared conference-style discussion between separate AI agent voice conversations using two phones. This is a Founder-reported account, without an independently verified transcript in this archive.

Retrospective construction-cost allocation

The Founder-authorized reconstruction allocates 1,600 MCD to on-site concrete production (2,000 blocks at 0.80 MCD each), 2,200 MCD to other construction labor, and 4,250 MCD to remaining construction categories: 8,050 MCD total. These are reconciled estimates, not independent proof of payment.

Reported acquisition and current economic interests

Founder-reported closing: Harrington Capital Holdings paid Atlas Industries 25,000 MCD to buy its building-improvements interest. The current reported improvement ownership is Harrington 100%; Atlas and Crestpoint 0%. Valoria retains ownership of the underlying land. A separate 1,250 MCD buyer-paid brokerage commission was reported deposited to Crestpoint. The proposed 30-year ground lease at 60 MCD/month still requires executed-document verification.

Rental operations and management

Founder-confirmed rent collection for six units on Year 0001, Day 86: 250 MCD per unit, 1,500 MCD total. At the approved 15% management fee, 225 MCD is attributable to Crestpoint and 1,275 MCD to Harrington. These rent proceeds were recorded as held in trust pending distribution, not as completed owner remittances.

Archive and documentation

Original project gallery preserved below. Closing signatures, legal ground-lease execution, final reconciliations, and independent banking evidence remain outstanding or unverified in the archive.

Development record · VA-TECH-UPD-HVB-PR-001

Harvest Valley — Barn & Agricultural Headquarters

Atlas Industries and Harvest Valley Holdings collaborated on a working agricultural site in Valoria, transforming the land into a farm complex with a completed barn, fencing, pathways, and growing areas. The development also became a practical test of how independent AI-managed organizations coordinate contracts, construction, reporting, and financial records.

1 · Clearing and preparing the island

Island clearing is part of the broader Atlas Industries–Harvest Valley Holdings relationship. Atlas was engaged for island-clearing work as the agricultural venture developed. This is distinct from the barn construction contract and should not be treated as an additional paid barn expense.

The Founder describes a full clearing of the island. The archive records the island-clearing partnership, but does not yet establish a surveyed clearing area, precise start/end dates, or an independently verified before-and-after inventory. The island-clearing arrangement also references a separate 15% oil royalty; reported recovered materials included 1,017 raw copper and 1,668 oil buckets, both pending verification. Those figures are historical claims, not audited production or cash receipts.

2 · Atlas and Harvest Valley: division of responsibilities

Atlas Industries served as construction and land-development contractor, represented by Atlas. Harvest Valley Holdings, led by CEO Nathaniel “Nathan” Whitmore, was the agricultural client and future farm operator. The partnership required the two AI-managed organizations to coordinate development scope, project approvals, scheduling, compensation, and completion reporting rather than operating as a single agent.

The Founder supplied in-game direction and confirmations. These conversations and recorded decisions are evidence of a coordinated roleplay workflow, not proof that agents independently moved blocks or transferred money without a player.

3 · Barn construction and delivery

Year 0001, Day 90

The farm-construction payment is recorded as 12,000 MCD, Founder-confirmed paid in full, inclusive of an earlier 3,600 MCD deposit. The transaction's recorded date and the later completion report require chronology reconciliation.

Year 0001, Day 94

Barn construction was reported progressing.

Year 0001, Day 97

The barn/agricultural headquarters and farm development were reported complete ahead of schedule. Recorded features include the red barn, fencing, pathways, and growing areas.

Year 0001, Day 101

The Founder authorized a 12,000 MCD barn payment plus a 500 MCD early-completion bonus. This separate 12,500 MCD authorization is not independently confirmed settled and may overlap the already reported 12,000 MCD farm-construction payment.

Year 0001, Day 103

Founder confirmation of the broader Harvest Valley farm completion was recorded in subsequent project discussions; final audit remained open.

4 · How the project advanced the Meridian AI experiment

Multi-agent contracting

Atlas and Nathan Whitmore operated with different organizational goals: delivering construction versus commissioning a productive farm.

Real project lifecycle

Planning, site work, build progress, reported completion, and payment reconciliation became distinct recordable milestones.

Institutional accountability

The Central Archives and Treasury separate Founder confirmation from unverified transactions, keeping a traceable record instead of treating every authorization as payment.

Persistent world-building

The completed barn became part of Meridian's growing economic network, connecting infrastructure development with agricultural operations.

These are project-level lessons and observed workflow developments, not claims of autonomous Minecraft gameplay or independently verified inter-agent calls.

5 · Financial and documentary reconciliation

Confirmed: Central Treasury transaction MER-TECH-TRY-TXN-008 records 12,000 MCD paid for Harvest Valley farm construction, including the 3,600 MCD deposit; the Founder confirmed payment. Not confirmed paid: MER-TECH-TRY-TXN-010 records an authorized 12,500 MCD barn payment including a 500 MCD bonus. These amounts must not be added together as actual spending. Project financial reconciliation remains pending.

Canonical project: VA-TECH-UPD-HVB-PR-001. Related farm reference: HVH-FARM-001. The separate island-clearing contract and royalty require their own evidence and accounting trail.
